note: Toc.js builds a client-side table of contents. Two surfaces: a per-content-type node extra field 'toc_js' and the toc_js_block block plugin. Per-content-type config is stored as node type third-party settings under 'toc_js' (toc_js_active + ~40 keys from TocJsService::defaultSettings(); defaults selectors h2,h3, container .node). Permission 'administer toc_js'. Requires node+block. No configure route/Drush. Introspection reads node-type third-party toc_js settings; execution enables the TOC + places the extra field, and places a toc_js_block. Uses namespaced content types (tocjs_*) and a namespaced block, no node operations (safe on this shared site).

evals.prompt: The Drupal Toc.js module can display a table of contents in two different ways. What are the two ways to add a Toc.js table of contents to a page?
evals.expected_output: 1) A per-content-type node extra field ('toc_js') that you enable on the content type and place in Manage display; 2) the toc_js_block block plugin ('Toc.js block') that you place in any region for any page.

evals.prompt: When you enable Toc.js for a content type in Drupal, where are those TOC settings (like whether it's active and the heading selectors) stored?
evals.expected_output: As third-party settings on the node.type.<bundle> config entity, under the 'toc_js' namespace: toc_js_active plus ~40 option keys (title, selectors, container, list_type, smooth_scrolling, etc.).

evals.prompt: By default, which headings does Toc.js turn into a table of contents, and where is the TOC actually generated?
evals.expected_output: By default it collects h2,h3 headings inside the .node container (defaults from TocJsService::defaultSettings()), and the table of contents is generated client-side in the browser by the toc.js JavaScript library reading data-* attributes.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site a content type with machine name tocjs_doc has Toc.js enabled. Inspect the live content type configuration and state the TOC title text that has been set for it.
evals.expected_output: node.type.tocjs_doc third_party_settings.toc_js.title is 'In this article' (and toc_js_active is true).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the content type tocjs_sel has Toc.js enabled with custom heading selectors. Inspect the live configuration and state the heading selectors it uses.

On this Drupal site the content type tocjs_page exists with Toc.js disabled. Using Toc.js, enable the table of contents for tocjs_page and place the Toc extra field on its default view display. Apply the changes to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set node.type.tocjs_page third_party_settings.toc_js.toc_js_active = TRUE (setThirdPartySetting) and save, then add the 'toc_js' extra field component to core.entity_view_display.node.tocjs_page.default and save.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, place a Toc.js block (the toc_js_block plugin) in a region so a table of contents is shown. Create it with id tocjs_testblock and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create a Block config entity with plugin 'toc_js_block' (id tocjs_testblock) placed in the default theme in a region (e.g. content), with settings including the toc_js.service defaultSettings, then save.
